findings.quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages
findings.rationale: The clause is mutual, excludes consequential damages on both sides and carves out Sections 13 (IP indemnity) and 14 (confidentiality), which matches the playbook's carve-out expectations. There is, however, no monetary cap at all, so our own direct-damages exposure is unlimited as well as Garman's. Because the asymmetry the playbook guards against (Customer uncapped / Vendor capped) is absent and unlimited Vendor liability favours us, we would not redline unilaterally, but flag for a commercial decision on whether to propose a mutual 12-month-fees / USD 1M cap.

findings.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees
findings.rationale: Garman gives an IP ownership/non-infringement warranty backed by an indemnity, with the usual procure/modify/replace remedies, which sits at the playbook fallback. Two points to note rather than redline: the ten-calendar-day claim-notice period is tight and ideally should be "prompt notice, and only to the extent prejudiced", and there is no indemnity for Garman's breach of law or wilful misconduct.

findings.quote: not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations
findings.rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction on our business. Section 3 contains only ordinary licence-scope restrictions on use of the Software, which the playbook does not treat as a restrictive covenant.

findings.quote: a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
findings.rationale: No exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation is imposed on us; we remain free to license competing software from other suppliers.

findings.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
findings.rationale: No most-favoured-nation obligation burdening us appears anywhere in the agreement.

findings.quote: both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party
findings.rationale: This is a no-hire (not a non-solicit) covering all of Garman's employees and binding our affiliates, with no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches. No-hire provisions are walk-away territory under our playbook; we narrow it to a mutual solicitation restriction limited to personnel involved in the services, with the standard carve-outs.

replacement.oldText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.
replacement.newText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision or receipt of services under this Agreement, provided that neither general advertisements or recruitment campaigns not specifically targeted at such employees, nor the hiring of any person who responds to such advertisements or who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis, shall constitute a breach of this Section.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We can accept a mutual, narrow non-solicit but not a no-hire: we have converted this to a solicitation restriction limited to personnel involved in the services, with the standard general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.

findings.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
findings.rationale: We have an unrestricted convenience right on 90 days' notice with no early-termination fee, and Garman has no convenience right — this sits at the playbook fallback (preferred is 30 days plus an express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is absent). Not worth a redline given the perpetual, fee-driven structure.

findings.quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule
findings.rationale: The licence is perpetual and maintenance runs in renewable one-year terms with no automatic renewal, no non-renewal notice window and no stated uplift mechanic. Nothing to redline; we should confirm the Fee Schedule does not contain an uncapped maintenance uplift.

findings.quote: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
findings.rationale: Nova Scotia is outside our accepted list (NY, DE, CA, England and Wales), but it is our own home jurisdiction — not Garman's (Saskatchewan) — and the venue is non-exclusive, so the clause does not create the foreign-forum risk the playbook targets. We would leave it unless the business prefers New York.

findings.quote: Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
findings.rationale: This is a blanket consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A carve-out and no reasonableness standard, which is walk-away territory: it would let Garman block or re-price on a sale of our business. We add the successor/affiliate carve-out and a reasonableness standard, keeping the clause mutual.

replacement.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
replacement.newText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; provided that either party may assign this Agreement, upon written notice to the other party and without consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a consent right over our own corporate transactions; we have added the standard affiliate/successor carve-out and a reasonableness standard, applied mutually. Section 3(c) should be read subject to this provision.

findings.quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto)... No title to the intellectual property in the Work is transferred to Sparkling by this Agreement.
findings.rationale: Garman retaining ownership of its own software is acceptable, and we receive a licence plus on-site source code and a perpetual fallback licence on default. Worth noting (not redlining) that Modifications built to our Schedule "D" specifications also vest in Garman, and that the agreement says nothing about ownership of our data — neither is a walk-away because no Customer IP or data is assigned to Garman.

findings.quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
findings.rationale: Affiliates are covered, but the licence is expressly non-transferable with no path to a successor in an M&A transaction and does not extend to contractors acting on our behalf (e.g. outsourced IT operating the AS400s). That fails the playbook fallback, which requires successor transferability.

replacement.oldText: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use:
replacement.newText: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling, affiliated companies of Sparkling and contractors acting on their behalf operating at Authorized Locations, a non-exclusive licence, transferable to a successor in connection with a merger, amalgamation, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of Sparkling's assets, to use:
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Our licences must reach contractors operating the systems for us and must follow the business in an M&A transaction; we have made those two minimal edits and left the scope otherwise unchanged.

findings.quote: Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder
findings.rationale: The agreement contains no audit, inspection or licence-verification right exercisable by Garman against us; the only examination right runs in our favour. This is the preferred position.

findings.quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
findings.rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties or early-termination charges are payable by us; termination for convenience carries no fee.

findings.quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
findings.rationale: A one-year (and, while maintained, evergreen) conformance warranty with a repair remedy exceeds the preferred 12-month software warranty, and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer anywhere. We note only that the remedy stops at best-efforts repair with no refund backstop and that there is no express no-malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty.

The agreement contains no insurance obligation, although Garman installs software on our systems, converts our data and attends our Authorized Locations. We insert a short general liability and E&O provision in the General Matters section (cyber cover omitted as Garman does not host our data).

replacement.oldText: (i) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
replacement.newText:
(i) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter, commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate, and professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000, and shall provide certificates of insurance to Sparkling on request.

(j) All paragraph headings contained in this Agreement are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.
replacement.comment: [Playbook] Vendors working on our systems and premises carry standard cover; we have inserted our baseline CGL and E&O limits (fallback: E&O USD 1M). Subsequent lettering to be renumbered.

findings.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
findings.rationale: No minimum purchase, take-or-pay or shortfall obligation appears in the body of the agreement. We should confirm Schedule "A" (not provided) contains no minimum maintenance commitment.

findings.quote: Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
findings.rationale: There is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on Garman. The risk is materially mitigated because this is an on-premises AS400 deployment (our data stays with us) and Section 16 gives us on-site source code plus a perpetual licence if we terminate for Garman's default. We would nonetheless ask for a short exit-assistance right (up to 6 months at then-current rates, including data extraction support) if the negotiation allows.
